- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast peak at 10–15% above recent high.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.80) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day for 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizons: if forecast is >1.5% above 10-day moving average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is mixed (0.27–0.53) and price is volatile, model tends to overpredict late-period values; cap forecast at 10% below 30-day true mean.
- If sentiment drops sharply after a forecast spike, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 1–2% per day for 3–5 days following sentiment drop.
